audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0, 3, 5 and 6 disagree with the mirror, and row 6 contradicts its own whys[6].
audit.why: The mirror set Skill, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Jax, Yasuo across both layers as one atomic group. Stored rows had Level 1 = Jax, Levels 4-5 = Skill, First item = Skill and 2+ items = Jax, while whys[6] says 'Only at 2+ items does your crit-and-R teamfight scaling finally flip the matchup to you' and phases[6].why says your pattern is at full power.

audit.whatIsWrong: Only two sequencing cues and no cooldown numbers.
audit.why: Leap Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, Empower 7/6/5/4/3, Counter Strike 17/15/13/11/9, Grandmaster-at-Arms 110/100/90, Last Breath 70/50/30.
audit.corrected: Numbers written into whys[0], spikes[0], spikes[1], early, mid, wants.you[1], phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two places tell you to Wind Wall Leap Strike or 'block a key auto'; the R is called Grandmaster's Might; Counter Strike's effect on Steel Tempest is never stated; 'Last Breath converts ANY knockup'.
audit.why: Leap Strike is a targeted dash with no projectile, and Jax's autos are melee — he has no projectile in any slot, so Wind Wall does nothing in this matchup at all. Saying it blocks 'a key auto' invites the player to spend a 25-second cooldown on nothing. Counter Strike dodges ALL incoming attacks, and Steel Tempest is explicitly treated as a basic attack, so your Q is dodged too — that is the decisive interaction. His ultimate is Grandmaster-at-Arms. Nothing lifts him airborne, so Last Breath only follows your own two-stack whirlwind.
audit.corrected: Wind Wall's irrelevance stated plainly; Steel Tempest named as dodgeable by Counter Strike; R renamed; Q2 whirlwind named as the only Last Breath setup.

audit.why: Jax's combo opens with an auto-attack reset on a 7s rank-1 cooldown — the wind-up is the cue to step back, not the ability cast.

edits.before: Jax out-trades you at levels 1-2 with superior auto range and Leap Strike while you lack an all-in.
edits.after: Level 1 is even — Leap Strike is 8s at rank 1 and he has no Counter Strike yet to punish you.

edits.before: Level 6 R Grandmaster's Might stacks resists and burst that outclass your R in a straight duel.
edits.after: Level 6 Grandmaster-at-Arms stacks resists and burst that outclass your R in a straight duel.

edits.before: At first item Blade/Trinity plus his kit make his in-range DPS peak, which Wind Wall can't shut off.
edits.after: At first item his in-range DPS peaks, and Wind Wall does nothing — Jax has no projectile.

edits.before: Jax spikes hard the moment he has E Counter Strike: any all-in where he leaps in with Q Leap Strike and holds E will stun you and eat your trades, so respect the Counter Strike window and never commit while it's up.
edits.after: Counter Strike (E) is 17s at rank 1 and dodges all incoming attacks before stunning — Steel Tempest counts as a basic attack, so it is dodged too. Never commit your Q stacks while E is up; wait out the dodge window first.

edits.before: Jax R Grandmaster's Might turns his auto-attacks into burst and stacks bonus resist every third hit; even after your R Last Breath the sustained fight favors him if E is up to shrug your Qs.
edits.after: Grandmaster-at-Arms (R) is 110s at rank 1: every third attack adds magic damage and the active stacks resists. Even with Last Breath the sustained fight favours him while E is up.

edits.before: Jax's first item (Blade of the Ruined King or Trinity) makes his DPS explode and your Wind Wall only blocks his auto once per fight — it doesn't stop his in-range beatdown, so this is his peak.
edits.after: His first item makes his DPS explode, and Wind Wall does nothing at all here — Jax has no projectile in any slot, so the wall never enters this matchup. This is his peak; concede the side lane.

edits.before: Only past two items does your snowball scale flip it: if you're fed with crit and R engage on his backline you outrange his single-target burst — an even Jax still wins the 1v1, so play for the teamfight.
edits.after: Only past two items does your scaling flip it: with crit and Last Breath off your own Q2 whirlwind you win the teamfight, while an even Jax still wins the straight 1v1 — so play the map.

edits.before: Jax owns levels 1-2: his auto range and Leap Strike out-trade your Q pokes, and you have no answer to a point-blank all-in yet. Last-hit under tower, don't walk up for Q casts, and keep Sweeping Blade for escape, not aggression. He wants you to greed a caster minion so he can Q-E onto you.
edits.after: Jax owns levels 2-3: his auto range and Leap Strike out-trade your Q pokes. Empower (W) is 7s at rank 1 and resets his auto — the wind-up is your cue to step back, not the cast. Last-hit safely, don't walk up for Q casts, and keep Sweeping Blade for escape rather than aggression.

edits.before: Through 3-6 this stays Jax's lane. Once E Counter Strike is online any dash you make into range risks the stun, and his R spikes his dueling well past yours. Wind Wall the Leap Strike or bait E on cooldown, but expect to lose short trades — respect his jungler because a gank plus his E all but guarantees your death.
edits.after: Through 3-6 this stays Jax's lane. Once Counter Strike is online any dash into range risks the stun, and his R spikes his duelling past yours. Wind Wall cannot touch Leap Strike — it is a targeted dash, not a projectile — so bait the 17-second E instead, and respect his jungler because a gank plus E is death.

edits.before: Jax stays ahead into his first item; Blade/Trinity plus Grandmaster's Might is his hardest window and Wind Wall can't stop an in-range beatdown. Only with two-plus items and a crit lead does your teamfight R engage overtake his single-target power — win the map, not the side lane.
edits.after: Jax stays ahead through his first item; Grandmaster-at-Arms plus a completed item is his hardest window, and Wind Wall answers none of it. Only with two-plus items and a crit lead does your teamfight R engage overtake his single-target power — win the map, not the side lane.

edits.before: Use Wind Wall to block his Leap Strike or a key auto in the all-in
edits.after: Bait the 17-second Counter Strike before you spend a single dash

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Jax's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Last Breath (70s at rank 1) fires only off your own Q2 whirlwind. Grandmaster-at-Arms is 110s and stacks resists.

edits.before: Last Breath converts ANY knockup into a kill window — build your teamfight around that. Jax carry threat: 10/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he gets ahead.
edits.after: Last Breath needs an airborne target and only your own Q2 whirlwind supplies one. Jax carry threat: 10/10 — shift to picks and wave control if he leads.

edits.before: - Jax Counter Strike: matchup-defining — Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Jax Counter Strike: 17s at rank 1 — it dodges attacks, Steel Tempest included, then stuns. - Empower is 7s and resets his auto. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.

edits.before: Dodges autos + stuns. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Dodges attacks, Steel Tempest included, then stuns. 17s at rank 1.

notes: Highest-value correction here: the page told the player to Wind Wall Leap Strike and 'a key auto'. Jax has no projectile in any slot, so Wind Wall is inert in this matchup — spending it is a pure loss. The other one worth flagging is that Counter Strike dodges Steel Tempest, since Riot's own Yasuo text says Q is treated as a basic attack. R renamed from 'Grandmaster's Might' to Grandmaster-at-Arms in two places.
